Two of my findings are new and neither has been reported by the six records already on
this branch. One of them is not about this pull request at all -- it is a defect in

=== NEW 1 (STRUCTURAL, REPO-WIDE, NOT THIS PR'S FAULT, AND DECISIVE FOR IT).
    A single DISAGREE record permanently reds lwb-lanes for that PR. Forever. ===
In scripts/lwb_lanes._review_ok, the verdict test
    if data.get("verdict") != "AGREE":
        errors.append(f"{rel}: verdict is ... want 'AGREE'")
appends to ERRORS, and main() does `if errors: return 1`. The verdict test also runs
BEFORE the staleness test, so a DISAGREE record that reviewed some long-superseded
commit still contributes a hard failure. Records are globbed from the whole
reviews/<pr>/ directory, so they accumulate and never age out.
ISOLATED, DECISIVE PROBE (working tree only, everything restored afterwards):
  A) added one valid AGREE record naming the reviewable head, DISAGREE records left
     in place              -> EXIT 1, 78 FAIL lines
  B) identical AGREE record, the six prior DISAGREE records temporarily moved aside
                           -> EXIT 0, "lwb-lanes check passed"
The AGREE record was byte-identical between A and B. The ONLY difference is the presence
of earlier reviewers' honest DISAGREE records.
CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: once any reviewer files a DISAGREE on a branch, that branch
can only ever go green if someone DELETES a prior reviewer's evidence, or the pull
request is abandoned and re-cut. This repository is already doing the latter -- #28 was
re-cut as #31, #38 as #39 -- and reviewers on this branch have explicitly refused to do
the former, correctly, because destroying a prior reviewer's record is falsifying
evidence. So the honest reviewing this gate exists to compel is the thing that bricks the
branch. MY OWN RECORD HERE MAKES THIS WORSE, and I am filing it anyway because filing a
false AGREE to keep a branch alive is the one thing worse. The fix belongs in
lwb_lanes._review_ok -- a non-AGREE record should not be an error, it should simply not
COUNT toward REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS (a stale DISAGREE especially so) -- and it
cannot be made by me: scripts/ is outside what I am authorised to write.

The claim was true when written. Commit 5e415c4 ("docs(handoff): regenerate LAST")
touches HANDOFF.md, which is neither reviews/ nor proof/, so it is not a record-only
commit and resolve_reviewable_head stops there. From that commit on, a record must attest

IS evidence the file was reviewed, the opposite of what it says. The commit added to obey
the ordering rule is the commit that falsified the document's statement about itself, and
nothing re-checked it. I flag this because the document's entire subject is the exactness
of self-claims: this is that same error class, one more level up, and it is the third
time in this one document's history. lwb-check-state-claims cannot catch it (it is not a
sha or a count), so only a reader can.
